Hi Oliver — great to hear from you and thanks for the context.

Attached is a short snapshot of our hosted IO pricing and an exportable rate summary (redwood_hosted_ratecard_v1.pdf, redwood_rate_summary.xlsx). Key points up front:

- Baseline per-1M token IO rates (hosted API):
  • Model tier: redwood-std family (general-purpose) — Input: $0.95 / 1M tokens, Output: $1.45 / 1M tokens
  • Model tier: redwood-large family (higher quality/longer context) — Input: $1.90 / 1M tokens, Output: $2.70 / 1M tokens
  • Model tier: curated open models (community variants we host) — Input: $0.60 / 1M tokens, Output: $0.95 / 1M tokens

- Included models: redwood-std-v1, redwood-lrg-v1, and a rotating catalog of validated open checkpoints (full list in the attached).
- Pilot discount guidance: for proof-of-value pilots at ~<10M tokens/mo we commonly offer a pilot credit structure (one-time credit covering ~50% of the first month) or a short-term pilot discount (10–20%) depending on use case and gating (SLA, redaction, PII handling).
- Committed tiers: 3/6/12 month commitments start at a list discount of 10% (3m), 15% (6m), and 20% (12m) applied to baseline IO rates — larger, multi-year commitments can be negotiated.

Next steps I propose:
1) I can generate a one-page commercial quote scoped to your 8M tokens/mo estimate (includes pricing, recommended model tier, and an outline of security/compliance).
2) If you want, schedule a 30m call to review model tradeoffs (quality vs cost) — happy to loop Engineering.

I'll attach the ratecard now. If Ben (cc) needs to build a formal quote in HubSpot I can flag the deal.
